nodes.text: Faust's Home
Faust comes home and flops down on the couch, grabbing a book to read. Joan is in the corner, looking over a painting.

opts.text: Look at the painting she's looking at.

nodes.text: It is one of his, leaned against the wall where the window light falls.
I like this one.
I thought you were supposed to be busy.
With proper motivation, I can do even the most horrible things quite efficiently.
So tell me about your day then.
Your world is strange, I don't know what to think of it.
How is it any different from your own?
Everything. It's overwhelming, really. You'd think my world primitive in most aspects. This world is more advanced than the ones we've come from yet backwards in so many ways.
I don't doubt it. We've got to find some measure of balance, I'm sure our history is no different when it comes to difficult compromise. Have to make sacrifices somewhere.
So are you a champion of your people?
Hah. Hardly. I try to be a good friend and family member, and only made good grades in school, pretty low requirements for championhood.
You say you are average, but you do not seem it.
I don't know what I am. Just when I think I'm something, life throws another labor at me to complete, and I'm something brand new.
So you are a champion.
The only trophies I have are my books, my friends, and my stories.
Joan sits next to him on the couch. She pulls out a dagger.
Your eyes may not be able to see the energies that reside within this blade, but you should be able to feel them.
Faust touches her blade.
It feels like warm skin.
That is because it is tied to my body and soul. When you touch my blade, you touch me.
Faust keeps his hand on the blade, looking Joan in the eyes. She leans in to kiss him.
We probably shouldn't.
How often are you given the gift of a woman from another dimension, blind champion?
Well, if I'm blind, perhaps you should guide the way.
What do you think I was trying to do, John Faust?
They kiss.
This can only mean trouble.
For you or for me?
For everything.
They kiss again.
